sources.entry: OpenRabbit - Free, open-source, self-hosted AI GitHub PR reviewer that runs entirely in GitHub Actions.

summary.one_liner: OpenRabbit is a free, open-source, self-hosted GitHub pull request reviewer that runs inside your own GitHub Actions and uses a pluggable LLM provider to post review comments.
summary.what_it_does: It analyzes PR diffs and sends them to an LLM provider (the README names Groq and OpenRouter, plus others via adapters), then posts a structured review with a summary and inline comments or suggestions. It can fetch extra project files when it lacks context and reads linked GitHub issues to understand intent. Review behavior is configured through the workflow, including review_mode (summary, inline, or both) and tone_mode. The README also describes a mentor-style "Socratic" tone, a performance/scalability check, a security auditor pass, suggestion validation, and DRIFT detection for unrelated changes that should go in a separate PR. The workflow runs on pull_request_target events (opened, reopened, edited, synchronize).
use_cases: automated code review on GitHub pull requests
self-hosted AI PR review without a SaaS subscription
catching security issues like SQL injection or XSS in PRs
getting inline review suggestions in CI
free AI code review using OpenRouter free models
how_to_run: Paste the workflow that uses aryanbrite/openrabbit@main, with github_token and llm_api_key inputs.
Set llm_provider (openrouter or groq) and llm_model (default example: openrouter/free).
Store your LLM API key as a repository secret named LLM_API_KEY under Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions.
Open or update a pull request to trigger the reviewer.
stack: LLM providers: Groq, OpenRouter (others via adapters in src/llm)
notable: Runs entirely in your own GitHub Actions runner with no central server or proxy
Default uses OpenRouter's free model pool, rotating between free models to handle rate limits
Two-stage file fetch and linked issue awareness to reduce context blindness
DRIFT detection flags unrelated changes and suggests moving them to a separate PR
Review modes: summary, inline, or both
caveats: The free OpenRouter pool is rate-limited and the README says it is not super reliable or consistent; a personal API key is recommended for better results
Requires an LLM API key stored as a secret
Uses pull_request_target, which runs with repository secrets and write permissions, so the workflow setup needs care
keywords: review my pull request with ai
alternative to third-party pr review bots
